home.exposed: `{path}` can be modified by other accounts of this computer, and Crisol runs and trusts what is inside it, so it will not go on
home.exposed_fix: `{path}` can be modified by other accounts of this computer, and Crisol runs and trusts what is inside it, so it will not go on. Remove their write access: {fix}

doctor.services.nothing_running: nothing is running; `crisol start` starts the services
done.databases_web_not_started: the web stack was not started: {reason}

ca.io_temp: cannot create a temporary file in `{path}`: {error}
ca.invalid: the local CA in `certs/` cannot be used: {reason}
ca.incomplete: `certs/` has `{present}` but not `{missing}`: restore the missing file or remove the other one and make a new CA (it must be trusted again)
ca.key_mismatch: `ca.key` is not the key of `ca.pem`. If a run of Crisol was interrupted while making the CA, remove both files and make a new one (it must be trusted again); if not, somebody changed one of them
ca.expired: the local CA expired; make a new one (it must be trusted again)
ca.already_exists: a local CA already exists in `certs/`
ca.tld_not_special_use: `.{tld}` is not a name reserved for local use (test, localhost, example, invalid, local, internal, home.arpa): a local CA is not made for it, because it could vouch for real public domains. Its sites are served over HTTP; use a TLD such as `.test` for HTTPS
ca.exposed: `{path}` can be modified by other accounts on this computer, so the local CA cannot be trusted. Remove write access for the other accounts on it (on Windows, `crisol doctor` shows the exact `icacls` command), or move CRISOL_HOME to a private folder and make the CA again
ca.not_covered: the local CA cannot issue a certificate for `{name}`: make a new CA (it must be trusted again)
system.exclusions_none: There were no Defender exclusions inside {home}

teardown.step.close_window: Close the Crisol window, which is open (also when it is only in the tray): its program and what it keeps cannot be deleted while it runs

teardown.step.autostart: Remove the entry that starts Crisol when you sign in ({command})

teardown.step.startmenu: Delete the Start menu entry that opens the window ({path})

teardown.problem.trust_open: cannot open the certificates you trust ({error}); to do it by hand, {by_hand}
teardown.problem.helper_unknown: cannot tell whether the helper is installed ({error}); `{command}` removes it

doctor.memcached: Memcached has no password (its login needs SASL, which this build does not have): it listens on 127.0.0.1 only, but any program or account of this computer can read and write everything in it. Do not keep PHP sessions in Memcached (SESSION_DRIVER=memcached, session.save_handler=memcached) if this computer has other accounts: anyone who can read the sessions can impersonate the users of your local applications. Use files, the database or Redis, which have a password.
